articles.title: BRUCE PEARL: Conservatives are attacking the very college sports bill that protects women
articles.summary: Retired Auburn coach says critics wrongly claim the Protect College Sports Act guts Title IX, warning that inaction threatens women's and Olympic sports programs.
articles.body: Men don’t belong in women’s sports. That isn’t complicated, but some conservative influencers and interest groups are allowing it to become complicated through careless claims about legislation designed to protect college athletics. I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts and win the larger fight for women, fairness and the future of college sports. Some organizations and women’s-sports advocates claim the Protect College Sports Act would "gut" Title IX or invalidate state laws that reserve women’s teams for women. They are wrong. The text says the opposite. REPORTER'S NOTEBOOK: COLLEGE SPORTS BILL ENTERS LEGISLATIVE 'RED ZONE' AS SEASON KICKS OFF Section 127 explicitly states that nothing in the bill will "override, modify, or amend" Title IX. Female athletes would retain their current legal protections and ability to bring sex-discrimination claims. Section 120 also protects athletes, employees and others from retaliation for reporting discrimination or participating in Title IX proceedings. I spent nearly five decades coaching college basketball. I know the difference between winning a possession and winning the game. Conservatives now face a similar choice: We can chase applause by attacking allies and mischaracterizing the bill, or we can unite around the facts. Critics also claim the bill would erase state laws keeping men out of women’s sports. It would not. The legislation establishes national standards for Division I and Division II competition on limited eligibility questions, including academics, professional status, legal violations, age and years of eligibility. It neither creates a federal right for men to enter women’s competitions nor pre-empts state laws establishing sex-based athletic categories. REPUBLICAN SENATORS FILE AMENDMENT TO STOP COLLEGE SPORTS BILL FROM OVERRIDING STATE WOMEN'S SPORTS LAWS The bill does not expressly create a federal right for biological males to compete in women’s sports, and Section 127 states that nothing in the bill overrides, modifies or amends Title IX. Critics seem to be grasping at anything and eager to disregard the Title IX provisions here. Especially since the Supreme Court ruled in June that schools may keep men out of women’s sports. It also requires governing bodies to enforce rules related to state and federal law and allows individuals to sue when the law is violated. CONGRESS MUST FIX THE PROTECT COLLEGE SPORTS ACT BEFORE GIRLS PAY THE PRICE The bill also gives schools a powerful incentive to invest in women’s and Olympic sports. It creates a $22.5 million athlete-retention fund and allows schools to unlock up to an additional $5 million through eligible NIL investments in women’s, Olympic and non-revenue sports. A school seeking the full $27.5 million retention allowance would first need to invest $5 million in those sports. That is an ingenious way to ensure continued investment in programs that might otherwise be left behind. And every year Congress waits, the financial pressure on college athletics grows, and the programs with the fewest resources become even more vulnerable. My 2025 Final Four team had a total NIL budget of approximately $4 million. By the 2027 Final Four, some teams could be operating with budgets approaching $30 million. Conservatives should debate legislation, demand improvements and scrutinize every line. But facts must guide us. Too many Washington organizations would rather score points against perceived rivals than secure lasting victories for women and college athletes. CRUZ AND CANTWELL REFUSE TO BEND TO SEC AND BIG TEN CONCERNS IN REVISED COLLEGE ATHLETICS LEGISLATION Outrage is easy; turning shared principles into law is harder. Infighting only helps the left, which has spent years undermining Title IX while conservatives battle over legislation that expressly preserves it. If we can’t unite and get this done, we will lose college sports as we know them, and women’s and Olympic sports will continue to be among the first casualties. The stakes extend beyond Title IX, and the crisis is no longer theoretical. Thirty-two Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between the announcement of the House settlement and May 2025. WRAL reported that more than 40 Division I Olympic-sports programs were cut between May 2024 and July 2025, even though 75% of American Olympians in 2024 competed in collegiate athletics. NCAA data Even the University of Arkansas, backed by SEC resources, announced plans to eliminate its tennis programs before donors intervened to save them. If programs at schools like Arkansas are vulnerable, imagine the danger facing smaller schools, women’s teams and non-revenue sports nationwide. CLICK HERE FOR MORE FOX NEWS OPINION Credit where credit is due: Sens. Ted Cruz, R-Texas, and Eric Schmitt, R-Mo., and others have stepped up to move this legislation forward. President Trump has also led from the front by restoring the biological meaning of sex in federal policy, taking action to save college sports and backing this bill. Now, those who claim to support the America First movement should get in the game, help Congress finish the job and deliver this win for women and college athletes. Congress now has the opportunity to take important steps to stabilize college sports, support educational opportunities for young women and men, and provide protections for the uniquely American experience of intercollegiate athletics. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP There is broad agreement that college sports cannot go on with no meaningful guardrails around eligibility, transfer policy and NIL oversight. The Protect College Sports Act is an important step in the right direction, and Congress needs to keep the positive momentum moving forward. Winning the point may feel good. Winning the war matters more.

articles.title: Smithsonian-linked museum in El-Sayed’s backyard puts America’s post-9/11 response on trial
articles.summary: A Smithsonian Institution affiliate in Dearborn features exhibits arguing Arabs suffered unfair treatment after the Sept. 11 attacks on America.
articles.body: DEARBORN, MI – Nearly 25 years after the Sept. 11 attacks, a Smithsonian affiliate in Michigan continues to use its 9/11 exhibits and anniversary programming to focus on discrimination and government actions in the attacks' aftermath, while giving less attention to the nearly 3,000 people killed that day, Fox News Digital found. The Arab American National Museum in Dearborn, Michigan, features an exhibit arguing that Arab Americans "suffered two-fold as a result of the tragic events of September 11th," both from the attacks themselves and from what the museum describes as unfair treatment by the U.S. government afterward. Since its founding, the museum has repeatedly hosted programs examining what it describes as discriminatory consequences of the U.S. response to 9/11. Fox News Digital visited the museum earlier this month, reviewed its exhibits and gift shop, and examined years of anniversary programming and federal funding records. The AANM has received hundreds of thousands of dollars in grant funding from the National Endowment for the Humanities and is also an affiliate of the Smithsonian Institution. The Smithsonian has been under intense scrutiny from conservative lawmakers in recent months for allegedly allowing political bias to influence its presentation of history. TRUMP V. SMITHSONIAN: A TIMELINE OF HOW THE WHITE HOUSE FIGHT OVER 'WOKE' HISTORY UNFOLDED One placard criticizes the government’s post-9/11 detention of immigrants investigated for possible terrorist links, noting that "virtually none were charged" in connection with terrorism. "The Arab American community suffered two-fold as a result of the tragic events of September 11th. As with all Americans, they suffered the horror and grief. However, Arab Americans were unfairly held responsible, yet not a single Arab American was found guilty of any connection to September 11th," it reads. On Sept. 11, 2001, 19 al-Qaeda terrorists hijacked four passenger planes, crashing two into the World Trade Center, and one into the Pentagon. Passengers and crew fought back aboard United Flight 93, the fourth plane, prompting the hijackers to crash the plane in Pennsylvania. The attacks killed 2,977 people and triggered the largest investigation in FBI history. The museum placard also argues that Arabs faced harsher immigration enforcement after the attacks, saying some were "deported for minor visa violations or petty offenses which previously would have been overlooked." HISTORIAN BLASTS SMITHSONIAN'S ACTIVISM SHIFT AFTER FIRST VISIT IN OVER A DECADE: 'COMPLETELY DIFFERENT PLACE' In the 11 months after the attacks, immigration authorities detained 762 noncitizens on immigration charges in connection with the FBI’s terrorism investigation, including for overstaying visas or entering the country illegally, according to a Justice Department inspector general report. The watchdog found that some detainees with no terrorism ties were treated harshly and held under unnecessarily restrictive conditions. Public opinion also showed a more complicated picture of the post-9/11 backlash. President George W. Bush publicly urged Americans not to blame Muslims for the attacks, and polling later suggested attitudes toward Muslim Americans actually improved in the immediate aftermath. The share of Americans who viewed Muslim Americans favorably rose from 45% in March 2001 to 59% in November, two months after the attacks, according to the Pew Research Center. Beyond its permanent exhibit, AANM has repeatedly used programming around the 9/11 anniversary to examine discrimination and law-enforcement policies affecting Arab and Muslim communities. The museum holds a "solidarity" town hall each year, where criticism of the American reaction to 9/11 is often the focus. The online description of the event does not mention the deaths connected to the attacks themselves, but rather "offers a safe space for communities to reflect and engage in dialogue about the harmful prejudices that Arab and Muslim (and anyone perceived to be Arab or Muslim) individuals face on both an individual and systemic level." One such town hall in 2018 examined "how communities of color have been targeted through the frame of national security and profiled as violent threats." A year later, the AANM’s annual town, which received support from the National Endowment for the Arts, criticized how "institutions and communities of color have been infiltrated" by law enforcement as well as how leaders of those groups have been "targeted" following 9/11. SMITHSONIAN AMERICA 250 EXHIBIT FEATURES 3X MORE LIBERAL ITEMS THAN CONSERVATIVE ONES The AANM was founded in 2005, partially in response to the increased scrutiny directed at the Arab American community following the attack on the World Trade Center. In addition to receiving well over half a million dollars in funding from the NEH over its lifetime to support its exhibits and educational programming, the museum also benefited from a $385,000 grant from the Department of Housing and Urban Development which helped it expand its physical footprint in 2013. It received further HUD funding, over half a million dollars, between 2017 and 2019 as well as at least $50,000 from the State Department between 2016 and 2017, according to annual reports published by the museum. Dearborn, where about 54.5% of residents are of Middle Eastern or North African descent, is a key political center in Michigan ahead of one of the country’s most competitive Senate races this year. Socialist-aligned Abdul El-Sayed, who is running for the Senate, drew strong support from the city earlier this month. The museum’s focus extends beyond its criticism of the U.S. response to 9/11. On Sept. 10 — the eve of the 25th anniversary of the attacks — the AANM is scheduled to host a screening of "Seeds for Liberation," a film that portrays Hamas’ Oct. 7 terrorist attack as part of a decades-long Palestinian "struggle" and places it within a broader history of "anti-imperialist and decolonial movements." During Fox News Digital’s visit earlier this month, a section of the museum was dedicated to art criticizing Israel's alleged "occupation" of Palestinian land. One piece of art, the word "wall" presented in a stylized print, accuses the Israeli government of perpetuating a system of "apartheid." The art installation broadly accuses Israel of targeting civilians in military operations, denying basic necessities to Palestinians and unjustly occupying land. FORMER DEMOCRATIC STAFFERS, DEI LEADERS SHAPE SMITHSONIAN LEADERSHIP AMID POLITICAL FIRESTORM One placard accompanying a sculpture states that Israel has killed more than 2,000 Palestinian children since Sept. 29, 2000, citing If Americans Knew (IAK). The placard’s sourcing is itself controversial. Some pro-Palestinian organizations have distanced themselves from IAK over allegations of antisemitism and ties to white supremacists, allegations the group has disputed. IAK also operates a news site that has published articles rejecting the designation of Hamas as a terrorist organization. Another placard attached to a sculpture pulls a quote from Defense of Children International Palestine, which the Israeli government designated as a terrorist organization in 2021. DCIP and human rights groups have disputed the designation. The museum gift shop also sells Palestinian-themed merchandise, including map-shaped magnets and key chains, coloring books promising to help children "explore Palestinian heritage" and keffiyehs. IN CHARTS: A VISUAL BREAKDOWN OF THE SMITHSONIAN'S BILLION-DOLLAR TAXPAYER-FUNDED BUDGET CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The AANM, Smithsonian, NEA and NEH did not respond to requests for comment after being reached by Fox News Digital on Friday. Smithsonian affiliates, like the AANM, are independently operated museums that maintain formal partnerships with the Smithsonian, providing them with access to artifact loans, educational resources and consultations from institutional experts. In recent months, the Smithsonian has faced mounting pressure from Republican lawmakers and the president over allegations that its museums advance left-of-center ideological causes through their exhibits. Officials have threatened funding cuts against the institution if it does not root out what the Trump administration characterizes as anti-American bias.

articles.title: Trump taunts Canada on renaming Lake Ontario the 'Lake America' amid rising border trade rift
articles.summary: Trump floats renaming Lake Ontario to "Lake America" and accuses Mark Carney of fabricating claims about French-language demands in trade talks.
articles.body: President Donald Trump escalated his war of words with Canada on Tuesday morning, floating a U.S. push to rename Lake Ontario "Lake America" and accusing Canadian Prime Minister Mark Carney of lying about the Trump administration's position on French-language protections. "The United States is giving serious consideration to changing the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America in that we don’t expect to [sic] doing much business with Ontario any longer," Trump wrote Tuesday morning on Truth Social. Trump followed with another broadside aimed directly at Carney, rejecting claims the U.S. had sought concessions affecting the French language during the countries' recently collapsed trade negotiations. A POPULAR COCKTAIL HAS A TRUMP TRADE PROBLEM YOU PROBABLY DIDN’T KNOW ABOUT "I would never interfere with Canadians speaking French!" Trump wrote. "In fact, I have never even thought of doing such a stupid thing." "This lie was made up by a weak and ineffective Prime Minister in an attempt to gain political support, which he has totally lost, from the people of Quebec," Trump added. "I love French Canadians!" The posts marked the latest escalation in an increasingly bitter dispute between Washington and Ottawa after trade negotiations broke down late last week, triggering a new round of tariffs and threats of retaliation between the longtime allies. OPINION: TRUMP MUST CLOSE THE BACK DOOR CHINA USES TO EXPLOIT NORTH AMERICAN TRADE "We were not prepared to compromise on the protection of the French language and our culture," Carney said Saturday while announcing the suspension of negotiations, adding that those issues were "never on the table" for Canada. Carney doubled down Monday while in Quebec, arguing that French-language protections viewed by the U.S. as trade irritants were fundamental rights in Canada. U.S. Trade Representative Jamieson Greer, however, disputed Carney's characterization, calling the French-language dispute a "funny, fake story" and saying the U.S. objection instead centered on requirements affecting American streaming companies. Ontario is Canada's most populous province and a key hub in the tightly integrated U.S.-Canadian auto industry. The Great Lake is shared by Ontario and New York, making Trump's proposed name change another provocative shot at America's northern neighbor as the economic standoff deepens. TRUMP JUST EXPANDED HIS TARIFF PLAYBOOK WITH A POWERFUL TRADE WEAPON NO PRESIDENT HAS EVER USED The president has previously used geographic names to make a political point, ordering the change of Gulf of Mexico to be called Gulf of America. Vice President JD Vance traveled to Maine on Monday and delivered a lengthy defense of the administration's hard-line approach toward Canada, accusing Ottawa of treating Chinese goods more favorably than products coming from its American neighbor. "They treat Chinese goods more fairly than they do the goods that come from the people of Maine: It’s insanity," Vance said during a question-and-answer session Monday in Brewer. "And what we’ve said to Canada is stop it." Vance said the two countries had appeared close to an agreement before negotiations fell apart, blaming Canadian officials for bringing what he described as unreasonable demands to the table at the last minute. Trump separately announced Monday that 50% tariffs on Canadian automobiles, auto parts, trucks and steel would take effect Jan. 1, 2027, accusing Canada of years of unfair treatment of American producers. "Canada has been ripping off the United States of America for years," Trump wrote Monday. Despite the sharpening rhetoric, Vance left open the possibility Monday that Washington and Ottawa could eventually return to the negotiating table. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I think that we should have a deal," Vance said. "We expect fairness in our trade policy."

articles.title: California sheriff doubles down on seizing ballots as state Supreme Court hears whether he must return them
articles.summary: Sheriff Chad Bianco still holds 650,000 seized ballots as the California Supreme Court weighs whether he must return them to state officials.
articles.body: Riverside County Sheriff Chad Bianco remains defiant as the California Supreme Court deliberates whether he has to return approximately 650,000 ballots he seized from a November 2025 special election on redistricting. The court heard arguments Monday from Bianco’s lawyers and from California, where the state’s Attorney General Rob Bonta launched a legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures in March, ordering him to return the ballots. Bianco, however, refused, arguing through his legal team that he had a legal obligation to investigate the ballots after receiving a complaint. "I did this, and this was legal," Bianco told reporters. "I went a different route. They are legal. Both routes are legal. It's just their side doesn't like the route I chose." DOJ DEMANDS 865K DETROIT BALLOTS, THREATENING POSSIBLE LEGAL ACTION Bianco is still holding the ballots, his lawyer Bradley Hertz told reporters Monday, arguing that they are evidence. CALIFORNIA ACCUSED OF BLOCKING FEDERAL VOTER ROLL AUDIT AS DOJ ESCALATES PROBE OF ELECTION FRAUD CLAIMS "The sheriff is holding that evidence, safeguarding it as a custodian for the court," Hertz said. The ballots are from a November 2025 special election in which state voters decided on Proposition 50, a legislative redistricting measure that passed by more than 3.4 million votes, according to the California Secretary of State. CALIFORNIA ELECTION LIMBO FUELED BY 4 PRESSURE POINTS DRAGGING OUT VOTE COUNT, EXPERT SAYS Bianco, however, appeared to question whether the official count was valid. "How strange, that now we have evidence that the machines counted something different than the ballots that we have, and an Attorney General runs in to stop that investigation so that we’ll never know," Bianco said outside the courthouse. CALIFORNIA DOGE LEADER SLAMS NEWSOM, BONTA OVER STATE’S MASSIVE FRAUD ISSUES: "EVERY DAY IS OPPOSITE DAY" In filing his March legal challenge to Bianco’s ballot seizures, Bonta joined the UCLA Voting Rights Project, which launched a separate legal challenge to Bianco’s actions. "This is a sheriff that – despite the clear language in the California constitution, and in California government code, providing me direct supervision, authority over him – failed to comply with it," Bonta told reporters outside the courthouse Monday. "He can read, he knows what it says, it makes his violations even more egregious," Bonta also said. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Bianco, for his part, challenged Bonta’s interpretation of California code. "If you take it word for word, in that context, it means that he has direct authority that if I’m not doing my job he can order me to do it and if I don’t do it he can do it for me. But he cannot stop an investigation." Fox News Digital contacted the UCLA Voting Rights Project, the Riverside County Sheriff's Office and the California Attorney General's Office for further comment. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Outgoing House Democrat Al Green files another impeachment resolution targeting President Donald Trump
articles.summary: Democratic Rep. Al Green of Texas, who lost a Democratic primary runoff earlier this year, filed a new resolution targeting President Donald Trump for impeachment.
articles.body: Rep. Al Green, D-Texas, who has repeatedly targeted President Donald Trump for impeachment, renewed his effort by filing a new impeachment resolution on Monday. "Our country and the lives of people within it are at risk as President Donald John Trump is a great threat to the United States democratic republic, its Constitution, and democracy, violating Article II, Section 1, Clause 8 of the United States Constitution and its mandate to faithfully execute the office of President of the United States and, to the best of his ability, preserve, protect, and defend the Constitution of the United States," the document declares. The resolution accuses Trump of "abusing the powers of the presidency by operating United States Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) and Customs and Border Protection (CBP) as his vicious, quota-driven, unaccountable paramilitary police forces, transgressing with anonymity and secrecy, assaulting people, committing and covering up unjustified killings of civilians (including Renée Good, Alex Pretti, Lorenzo Salgado Araujo, and Johan Sebastián Durán Guerrero) with impunity (acting as judge, jury, prosecutor, and executioner), terrorizing communities, and brazenly and wantonly devolving the United States democratic republic into an authoritarian regime, where unjustified killings and coverups by ICE and CBP are normalized." AL GREEN RESPONDS TO JULY 4 QUESTION WITH RENEWED CALL TO IMPEACH TRUMP In a statement provided to Fox News Digital on Tuesday, White House spokeswoman Lauren Bis said, "This type of garbage is contributing to our law enforcement officers facing a more than 1,300% increase in assaults against them. The brave men and women of ICE and CBP put their lives on the line to arrest murderers, rapists, pedophiles, gang members, and terrorists. Al Green should be thanking President Trump and our law enforcement for delivering the largest decrease in violent crime in American history." Fox News Digital also reached out to the Department of Homeland Security, ICE and CBP on Tuesday. Given that Republicans currently hold the majority in both chambers of Congress, his latest impeachment push likely won't succeed. REP. AL GREEN TELLS HOMELAND SECURITY SEC. MULLIN TO 'SHUT UP' AFTER CALLING HIM A RACIST AT HEARING But in a letter to the president, Green said, "Mr. President, I am well aware of the fact that you will be defended by persons who will say, ‘The House won’t impeach, and if it did, the Senate won’t convict.’ Sir, my response is that articles of impeachment that are not approved by Congress can express on-the-record disapproval of presidential actions and demonstrate that there are some of us watching and willing to act." Green has fielded impeachment resolutions multiple times across both of Trump's White House terms. The congressman, who has served in the House since 2005, lost a Democratic primary runoff to Rep. Christian Menefee in May. TRUMP COULD FACE IMPEACHMENT IF DEMOCRATS SEIZE HOUSE MAJORITY, GOP LEADER WARNS CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The House impeached Trump twice during his first term but in both cases the Senate vote did not meet the threshold necessary for conviction. The Senate's vote on the second impeachment took place after Trump had already departed from office.

articles.title: ‘Send help’: LA GOP leader issues desperate appeal after Dem mayor’s campaign vid shocks viewers
articles.summary: LA County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge says Karen Bass's viral 6-to-1 matching funds video reveals how Democrats codified electoral 'shenanigans' into law.
articles.body: EXCLUSIVE: Los Angeles County GOP Chair Roxanne Hoge issued an impassioned appeal for Republicans to "send help" to Democratic-controlled California, describing what she sees as rampant corruption in the state and saying most people "can't understand the level of obsession they have with controlling our lives." In an interview with Fox News Digital, Hoge addressed the online reaction to a recent viral video posted by Democratic Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass in which the mayor said the city government would match six times every dollar donated to her re-election campaign. While some social media users expressed shock, Hoge said she was not surprised. "The rest of the country doesn't understand what we're living under here," she told Fox News Digital. "The number one thing people need to understand about Los Angeles in particular and California in general is that they've codified all of their shenanigans," she explained. "What normal people consider cheating or weirdness in the electoral process? It's all in the rules [here]." LOS ANGELES PROPOSAL TO ALLOW NONCITIZENS TO VOTE IN LOCAL ELECTIONS SPARKS ONLINE BACKLASH In a recent viral social media post, Bass, Los Angeles’ 72-year-old progressive mayor, said that "when you donate to our campaign, the city can match your donation 6 to 1," adding, "If you donate $5, the city turns it into $35." Bass said that "thanks to LA’s super match program, every qualified donation from Los Angeles residents is matched six to one by the city." She added that after this year’s mayoral primary, in which Republican candidate Spencer Pratt garnered significant support, "we had to start over from scratch." "So, we need you to rush in your matching donation right now, to help fuel this campaign," she said. Social media users questioned and criticized Bass’ comments. Conservative activist Billboard Chris commented, "How is it legal to take money from Los Angeles taxpayers to fund your own re-election campaign?" Commentator Matt Van Swol wrote, "Can someone please explain to me like I’m 5 years old how this is not COMPLETELY illegal?????" KAREN BASS RIPPED AFTER SUGGESTING TAXPAYER-FUNDED DENTAL CARE FOR METH USERS Author Michael Shellenberger simply wrote, "This is grotesque." "Is this a JOKE?!?" wrote well-known Los Angeles doctor and political commentator Houman David Hemmati. "Why on EARTH are LA City taxpayers, who can’t even afford to clean up their streets or have water in their fire hydrants, forced to match contributions to Bass’ Mayoral reelection campaign 6:1?!? … HUH?! Insanity!" Hoge, however, said the matching-funds program Bass describes in her campaign video is legal under city law. Los Angeles voters approved a public campaign-financing system in 1990 that the City Council later expanded into today’s six-to-one matching-funds program. Donations are subject to caps and eligibility rules. SIGN UP TO GET THE POLITICS NEWSLETTER "Voters passed something that sounded so good; they always sound so good at the beginning. Public financing matching funds for campaigns on a one-to-one basis. That seems great, right?" she said. "And then it transmogrifies … into what we have today, this many-headed hydra of insanity where taxpayers are on the hook for $6 for every dollar raised by a city of L.A. candidate." She noted that the rule applies not only to mayoral campaigns but also to City Council campaigns, adding that they "Have many active [Democratic Socialists of America] members currently sitting and running." Hoge said "the message that Karen Bass is sending is the same message that those of us who live here behind the blue curtain have been getting for decades." "And that is, ‘Forget it, Jake, it's Chinatown. Don't try to go against City Hall,’" she said. SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES' "We saw Spencer Pratt mount a very strong argument for sanity and good governance. It wasn't partisan, what he was saying. It was pure common sense, and they rose up because they were threatened." Fox News Digital reached out to Bass’ campaign and office for comment. Despite California’s political landscape, Hoge urged Republicans not to write off America’s most populous state as a lost cause. "California is totally worth fighting for because it is an absolute gem," she said, adding, "We are living with people who gleefully would reach into the shower and change the temperature while you're having a bath." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Addressing Republicans directly, she said, "We belong to the leave me alone party." "California, being in the west, is the ultimate place where you should be free to write your own story. And that, I think, is the number one thing people have to remember," she said. "They need to send help."

articles.title: Judge rejects Ghislaine Maxwell’s bid to toss conviction and warns against further appeals
articles.summary: The judge ⁠said that Maxwell’s claims were ​meritless and that any further appeal wouldn’t be taken in good faith.
articles.body: A judge rejected Ghislaine Maxwell’s bid ​to throw out her conviction ‌and 20-year prison sentence for helping the late financier Jeffrey Epstein sexually abuse teenage girls. In ​a decision made public on ​Tuesday, U.S. District Judge Paul Engelmayer ⁠said Maxwell’s claims were all ​meritless, and all or almost all were ​frivolous. Maxwell, 64, who represented herself, challenged her December 2021 conviction and sentence in Manhattan ​federal court and sought a writ ​of habeas corpus declaring her punishment unlawful. Prosecutors said ‌her ⁠latest claims were baseless or filed too late. Maxwell said many documents disclosed earlier this year through the Epstein ​Files Transparency ​Act ⁠show that her due process rights were violated because ​lawyers representing Epstein’s accusers served ​as “De ⁠Facto Prosecutors and agents of the government.” But the judge said this supposedly “new” ⁠evidence was largely irrelevant to ​Maxwell’s case. Engelmayer said Maxwell imposed a culture of silence among the staff at Epstein’s multiple homes as the “lady of the house.” Engelmayer said she and Epstein used methods commonly used by child predators and that Maxwell herself participated in such acts. Engelmayer said Maxwell has not made a substantial showing of a denial of a constitutional right, an appellate review is not warranted and any further appeal would not be taken in good faith.

articles.title: Ohio man charged over graphic threats to kill Trump, behead GOP lawmaker
articles.summary: The FBI arrested an Ohio man who allegedly sent graphic death threats to Jewish Republican Rep. Randy Fine and President Donald Trump via email.
articles.body: An Ohio man was arrested by the FBI after allegedly making graphic threats against a Jewish Republican congressman and calling for the death of President Donald Trump. Alex Justin Miller, 26, is accused of sending a "true threat" to Rep. Randy Fine, R-Fla., and his family, according to the Department of Justice (DOJ).  A copy of the message separately obtained by Fox News Digital shows Miller allegedly called Fine and his family "Nazi f—-s" and said he would burn their house down, pledging he would "never stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House." His message ended with "DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP." Miller was charged with interstate transmission of a threat to injure by the U.S. Attorney in the Middle District of Florida and faces up to five years in prison if convicted, the DOJ said. FAA EMPLOYEE CHARGED WITH ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL PRESIDENT TRUMP IN EMAIL TO WHITE HOUSE The incident was investigated by the FBI and the Brevard County Sheriff's Office with assistance from the Secret Service and Capitol Police, the DOJ said. "It was so graphic. It says, 'I'm gonna murder you. I'm going to cut your head off. I won't stop,'" Fine told Fox News Digital. "I reported it immediately. I unfortunately have learned what the difference is between a nasty message and a death threat, and this clearly was a death threat." The full message read: "Dear fat--- piece of s---stain, I cannot wait to take a trip to you lovely home and light the whole place on fire and murder you and your entire family in the middle of the night while you sleep. I hope you disgusting Nazi f---s sleep with one eye open for the rest of your life because I will NEVER stop until your head is hanging from the rooftops of the White House. You deserve 10000% to be beheaded and have your body paraded through the streets. DEATH TO RANDY FINE AND DEATH TO DONALD TRUMP!!"  Fine said he received the threat via email on the morning of primary Election Day in the Sunshine State. He also said it reinforced his belief that federal officials need more protection. "I don't know what this person's motives were for writing this, but it's someone not from Florida. So, you know, this was not a local constituent that was upset," he said. "I do think members of Congress need more security than we oftentimes get." FLORIDA MAN ARRESTED FOR ALLEGEDLY THREATENING TO KILL TRUMP, RUBIO AND BONDI He added that law enforcement found and arrested the man within 36 hours. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "I'm incredibly grateful to the U.S. attorney, the FBI, the Capitol Police, and all the law enforcement in Florida who took this seriously. The bottom line is, don't do this. Don't write messages like this to elected officials, Republican or Democrat. You want to call us bad people? Be my guest, but do not do this sort of thing," Fine said.

articles.title: El-Sayed’s ‘ding-a-ling’ defense of child sex changes becomes instant attack magnet: ‘Not the same, Abdul!’
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed's comparison of circumcision to child sex changes on Jesse Watters' show drew backlash from both left and right-leaning critics.
articles.body: Michigan Democratic Senate nominee Abdul El-Sayed is catching flak from across the political spectrum for comparing circumcision to child sex changes during a Monday night appearance on Jesse Watters Primetime. "So you think it’s okay for a parent to slash his kid’s ding-a-ling off?" Watters asked El-Sayed. "Are you circumcised?" El-Sayed asked Watters. ABDUL EL-SAYED GRILLED ON PAST STATEMENTS ON SHARIA LAW AND WHITE SUPREMACY, TAXING THE RICH "Circumcision’s different than castration," Watters responded. "It’s a problem that you think you get to decide what happens between a parent, a doctor and a patient," El-Sayed went on. "I’m just saying that, yes, circumcision is surgery on a kid’s ding-a-ling." Even some on the left didn’t buy into El-Sayed’s attempt to compare sex changes with circumcision. "This talking point isn’t it,"Ryan Grim, a co-founder of the left-wing outlet DropSite News, wrote in response to a clip of the exchange. SOCIALIST INSURGENTS EYE MIDWEST GAINS AS DEM CIVIL WAR THREATENS MUST-HOLD SENATE SEAT "I’m actually agreeing with Jesse Waters…" Andrew Laufer, a New York-based civil rights attorney, posted. "Abdul El-Sayed just compared circumcision to chopping a kid's entire penis off. Circumcision and castration are not the same, Abdul! Play this on repeat through November," Turning Point USA spokesperson Andrew Kolvet wrote. "He might be worse than Kamala Harris," conservative pundit Benny Johnson posted. "Holy crap, Abdul El-Sayed said circumcision is similar to sex change operations on minors," OutKick founder Clay Travis wrote. Others took opportunities to poke fun at El-Sayed for asking a news host about his penis during a nationally televised interview by making puns. "Interested to see El-Sayed's pole numbers after this," Washington Free Beacon reporter Chuck Ross quipped. Some, however, took a more serious tone. "Sex-rejecting surgeries are not comparable to circumcision, and everyone on this planet knows that, including El-Sayed," the senior policy director of the right-of-center organization Do No Harm said. "Candidates who choose to die on this hill will deserve their election losses." VETERAN PEDIATRICIAN HAILS MEDICAID SHIFT ENDING YOUTH SEX-CHANGE TREATMENTS: 'THIS IS NOT DENIAL OF CARE' "El-Sayed obviously knows the difference between circumcision and castration," Singaporean journalist and activist Melissa Chen wrote. "He just can’t say it out loud without pissing off the trans activists who make up his base now … Because he is locked into defending every absurd piece of gender ideology, he can’t actually answer Jesse Waters’ simple question of whether he supports gender-affirming care for under 18 year olds." Circumcision is an elective surgical procedure that is generally performed on infants, though some medical experts and critics have raised concerns about consent, medical necessity and the risks associated with the procedure. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP The El-Sayed campaign did not respond to a request for comment when reached by Fox News Digital on Tuesday.

articles.title: Dem who urged scandal-plagued candidate to quit now mourns his downfall in pivotal Maine race
articles.summary: Troy Jackson says he wished nothing had happened to Graham Platner but felt compelled to carry the progressive torch against Susan Collins in Maine.
articles.body: Maine’s newly anointed Democratic Senate nominee wished "nothing would have happened" to his predecessor, Graham Platner, whose campaign was torpedoed by sexual assault allegations last month. Troy Jackson, a former logger and Maine State Senate president, slid into the role as Democratic nominee after Platner’s insurgent campaign rapidly unraveled as scandal after scandal piled up, culminating in a sexual assault allegation from his ex-girlfriend that he has since denied. Jackson had previously run in Maine’s gubernatorial contest, finishing third in the primary earlier this summer. Once Platner exited the race in July, he was quickly chosen by Maine Democrats to succeed him to take on longtime incumbent Sen. Susan Collins, R-Maine, in a race that could define the balance of power in the Senate. BERNIE-BACKED MAINE DEMOCRATIC SENATE HOPEFUL SQUIRMS OVER PAST GRAHAM PLATNER SUPPORT But Jackson never really wanted to run for the Senate, the Midcoast Villager reported, but felt it was important to pick up the mantle of progressive politics that Platner had suddenly dropped. "I wish nothing would have happened with Graham," Jackson said. "I wish, you know, things would have continued like all that. It would have been much better. But when it did, I just didn't want to see all these people that are looking for somebody to fight for them go away once again broken and hopeless." Jackson, a fellow progressive who had previously worked on Sen. Bernie Sanders’, I-Vt., presidential campaigns, had campaigned alongside Platner and was endorsed by him in his bid for the governor’s mansion. PLATNER DROPS OUT OF CRUCIAL SENATE RACE AFTER BOMBSHELL RAPE ALLEGATION TORPEDOES CAMPAIGN When the final allegation hit, he, like several other Democrats both in-state and across the country, called on Platner to exit the race. "The allegations against Graham Platner are serious, credible, and deserving of full accountability — they cannot and must not be ignored," Jackson said in a statement on X at the time. "There is a powerful movement of working-class people in the state of Maine," he continued. "For the sake of that movement, and the millions of Americans who have put their trust in it, Graham must now step down." Jackson has had his own scandals, however. He has most recently come under scrutiny for his temper following a water bottle-throwing incident while he served in the Senate, and after the discovery of a 1988 police record in which Jackson was alleged to have assaulted a man and pushed his longtime partner, Lana Pelletier, who according to records is his second cousin, during a late-night confrontation. SUSAN COLLINS DROPS BRUTAL REMINDER OF DEM RIVAL ROCKED BY ACCUSATIONS Collins declined to weigh in on the police record when asked by Fox News Digital earlier this month, arguing that was up to Jackson. "But I will say that, based on widespread reporting, it appears that he struggles to control his temper," Collins said. Meanwhile, there’s an effort afoot to get Platner to register as a write-in candidate in Maine. The deadline to do so is Aug. 25. A website, writeingrahamforme.com, was launched as op-eds by Scott Niemi have made the rounds in local newspapers in Maine pushing for Platner to submit himself as a write-in, given that under Maine law write-in votes for an undeclared candidate don’t count. CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP Niemi argued in the Bangor Daily News that writing in Platner would prove to establishment Democrats that they don’t get to "overrule the will of Maine voter," and that because of Maine’s ranked-choice voting system, they could rank Jackson second to "keep the seat competitive." "If Graham does not have enough votes to advance during tabulation, those ballots are not wasted, they transfer over to Jackson in the next round if he is ranked second," Niemi wrote. "I believe it is a mathematically solid plan to defeat Collins come election time."

articles.title: Clinton’s eyebrow-raising socialism take sparks brutal mockery: ‘Definition of insanity’
articles.summary: Hillary Clinton called the Democratic Party's embrace of socialism a "healthy" experiment to reach young voters, sparking fierce backlash on X.
articles.body: Former Secretary of State Hillary Clinton called the Democratic Party’s current "experiment" amid the rise of democratic socialist candidates "healthy," drawing swift conservative backlash from critics who accused her of embracing the party’s socialist wing. "The Democratic Party right now is, I think, going through a kind of experiment, like who can actually respond particularly to young people's very real concerns about where they are at this point in their lives and what kind of future do they have for themselves? I think that is healthy," said Clinton. Clinton, a matriarch of the Democratic Party, defeated democratic socialist Sen. Bernie Sanders in the 2016 presidential primary. Her remarks come as socialist candidates increasingly challenge establishment-backed Democrats in races across the country. Clinton spoke Monday in conversation with the Hamptons Institute, weighing in on the Democratic Party’s ideological direction as it searches for ways to connect with younger voters while democratic socialist candidates have increasingly notched wins during the primary season. SHOCKING PERCENTAGE OF DEMOCRATS IDENTIFY AS 'DEMOCRATIC SOCIALISTS' ACCORDING TO NEW POLL: 'TOXIC POLICIES' The moderator asked Clinton where she sees the future of the Democratic Party as it undergoes a "major upheaval between center-left and democratic socialists" during their conversation on diplomacy, national security and global leadership. Conservative critics seized on Clintons' remarks, accusing her of embracing the Democratic Party’s socialist wing and invoking her failed 2016 presidential campaign. "INSANE Hillary Clinton says the Democrat Party is ‘going through an experiment’ to see if far-Left, socialist candidates — who want to abolish prisons and borders — can win over young voters," the Republican National Committee posted on X. "Run again in 2028. Do it," social media influencer Jack Posobiec posted. "Easy for her to say when she has her own security team," said Heritage Foundation media fellow Tim Young. "Hillary Clinton believes Democrats are "going through an experiment" to see if a new crop of further-left candidates can actually win young voters. The problem? Dems who want to abolish prisons and borders. She’s watching her own party test how far left it can push before the rest of the country walks away. It's basically a live experiment with the electorate at this point," X user Mario Nawfal posted.  DEMOCRATS LURE ‘POLITICALLY HOMELESS’ GEN Z TOWARD SOCIALISM — A COUNTERATTACK IS TAKING SHAPE "The Democrats only want to win, no matter the cost! If their actions of going far, far left send the country into ruins, they don’t care! They know that socialism has never worked, nor ever will work. Hillary may be a lot of things (a lot of which I can’t say on here), but she will pull out all stops to try and win. It doesn’t always work, like in 2016, but she will try anything to win…..no matter the consequences," said one user. "Say WHAT?! Hillary Clinton says the Democrat Party is 'going through a kind of experiment' by embracing socialist candidates to see if it will bring in younger voters - say it's 'healthy' This is the definition of insanity," the Conservative Brief posted. During her remarks, Clinton also turned the socialism charge back on President Donald Trump, accusing his administration of practicing what she called "socialism for the rich." "I get very amused when I hear Trump and his people talking about socialism and communism. The way he’s behaving is socialism for the rich. It is the most ridiculous administration when it comes to doing everything possible to avoid risks and loss for people who are already doing them and to use the power of the government to benefit himself and his cronies and his allies," said Clinton. SOCIALIST SURGE: MAMDANI FLEXES GROWING POLITICAL MUSCLE AS HE TAKES ON DEM ESTABLISHMENT Trump has increasingly used the rise of democratic socialists as a midterm attack line, labeling recent left-wing Democratic winners "hardcore, godless communists."He separately warned in June that New York City Mayor and democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani's rent-freeze policy would cause New York apartment buildings to deteriorate into "ghettos and slums." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "President Trump is creating good-paying jobs, securing trillions of dollars in investments, and positioning our country to dominate the remainder of the 21st century," White House spokesperson Davis Ingle told Fox News Digital. "Meanwhile, Crooked Hillary Clinton is still whining about her spectacular 2016 election defeat. It’s time for Hillary to move on," Ingle added.

articles.title: Muslim Brotherhood-linked networks embedded across Canadian institutions, new report alleges
articles.summary: A new report alleges Muslim Brotherhood-aligned networks have embedded themselves in Canada's elections, universities and civil society institutions.
articles.body: A new report is warning that networks aligned with the Muslim Brotherhood have become deeply embedded in Canada, raising concerns that Islamist influence taking root north of the border could pose a broader threat to the U.S. and Western democracies. A report from the Institute for the Study of Global Antisemitism and Policy (ISGAP) revealed ties between Muslim Brotherhood-aligned groups and Canadian democratic institutions, civil society, electoral politics and higher education, demonstrating similarities with other activist movements in the West, a phenomenon some analysts have described as the "red-green alliance." "Canada's challenge is not simply the presence of individual extremist voices or isolated institutional weakness. The report maps how interconnected ideological networks acquire legitimacy, institutional access, public funding, political influence and protection from scrutiny," Charles Asher Small, the research institute's executive director, told Fox News Digital. TURKEY’S NATO ROLE UNDER SCRUTINY AMID NEW REPORT ON HAMAS, MUSLIM BROTHERHOOD TIES Small warned that Canadian democracy traditionally has been rooted in openness, notions of citizenship, civil liberties and public trust but has since faced a dynamic of malign foreign influence that could promote ideological entryism, antisemitism and efforts to weaken democratic accountability. The roughly 200-page report, titled, "Assault on Democratic Values and Principles: How Islamist Entryism Weakens Civil Society and Higher Education in Canada," claimed "numerous apparent links" between the Muslim Association of Canada, a nonprofit based in Mississauga, Canada, and the Muslim Brotherhood, an organization established in Egypt in 1928 by ideologue Hasan al-Banna as part of a wider vision to create a global Islamic caliphate governing nations with rigid interpretations of Islamic law, rules and regulations from the majority Sunni sect. WATCHDOG UNLEASHES DATABASE TO EXPOSE 'LOOPHOLES' AS $5B IN FOREIGN CASH FLOODS US NONPROFITS The report alleged that leaders of the Muslim Association of Canada, one of the largest Muslim charitable organizations in Canada, operating mosques, community centers, schools and educational programs, were "directly or indirectly" associated with the Muslim Brotherhood and that those relationships could influence the charitable organization’s activities. "The ISGAP report is nothing more than recycled Islamophobic tropes dressed up as research. It is a biased, unsubstantiated hit piece that relies on discredited allegations that were themselves challenged by the Ontario Superior Court for their apparent bias," the Muslim Association of Canada told Fox News Digital in a statement. "The CRA audit has been completed. Preliminary questions raised around any links to the Muslim Brotherhood were dismissed from the CRA’s final conclusion," the statement added. "MAC is a solely independent Canadian organization. The ISGAP report amplifies narratives designed to fuel Islamophobia and sow division within Canadian society." Canadian tax authorities clashed with the Muslim Association of Canada in a 2023 audit, saying that there were indications of ties to the Muslim Brotherhood. The association denied these claims, citing systemic bias and "Islamophobia." HOUSE COMMITTEE PASSES FOREIGN FUNDING TRANSPARENCY ACT TO EXPOSE FOREIGN DONATIONS TO NONPROFITS The Canada Revenue Agency ultimately did not revoke the Muslim Association of Canada’s tax-exempt charitable status. The report alleged that Canadian groups affiliated with the Muslim Brotherhood assisted in influencing Canada’s election system, noting how a coordinated "Vote Palestine" campaign secured endorsements from 344 candidates across four political parties in Canada in the 2025 cycle. Fox News Digital sat down with Small, who said the report’s findings served as a warning sign for potential influence in the U.S. "The radical left wants to weaken Western or American hegemony, as does radical political Islam," Small explained. "Radical political Islam wants to rid the Islamic world of any influence of the United States, of Europe, of Christianity, of Judaism in its region to ethnically cleanse it." articles.title: Inside Gavin Newsom’s private mansion on sale for $7.5M
articles.summary: The governor is selling the property he lived in during his two terms in office, only months ahead of his leaving the post.
articles.body:
California Governor Gavin Newsom has listed his private mansion in Sacramento for sale for $7.5 million, double the price he and his wife, Jennifer Siebel Newsom, bought it for seven years ago.

The property in Fair Oaks has served as the Democrat's base during his two terms in office, and its sale comes mere months before Newsom officially steps down in January 2027.

Many have speculated about Newsom's possible run for the presidency in 2028, though the governor has not confirmed whether he will be a candidate for the nation's top job or not. The sale of his California home is only likely to fuel rumors there will be an impending presidential campaign announcement.

The Newsoms purchased the 12,000-square-foot Sacramento mansion in 2019 to avoid living in the official governor's mansion, a 150-year-old property, which, until Jerry Brown decided to move into it in 2015, had been serving as a museum. An exception was the stay of Ronald Reagan, who lived there for a few months in 1967.

The mansion at 7640 Tobia Way is only 15 miles from the state Capitol, making it easy for Newsom to commute to work. When the governor bought it as a "more kid-friendly" alternative to the official Victorian home, he paid $3.7 million for it.

That was just before historically low borrowing costs during the pandemic sparked a home-buying frenzy all across the country which, clashing with chronically low inventory levels, sent prices through the roof. We do not know if, since 2019, Newsom has implemented any upgrade or changes to the home.

The mansion, built in 1984, boasts several high-end amenities including a resort-style pool, a private tennis court, a cold plunge pool, and a 5,000-bottle wine cellar with its own tasting room. It has seven bedrooms and nine bathrooms, as well as three partial ones.

The sale is being managed by Matthew Hindy and Nick Sadek with Sotheby's International Realty. "It's a beautiful property. It's been well maintained and holds a special charm," Hindy told Newsweek in a written statement.

The listing describes the property as "an extraordinary showcase of Santa Barbara-inspired architecture […] privately positioned along the bluffs on 8.2 acres, where sweeping views and exceptional privacy create a truly rare setting."

According to the agent, "the residence offers an unparalleled combination of grandeur, comfort, and effortless entertaining."

The home's primary bathroom features two walk-in closets, dual showers and water closets, and a luxurious soaking tub, in what the listing describes as a "spa-like experience."

Outdoors, the home features a private pool, cold plunge, and hot tub. There is also a four-car garage.

"Some homes are beautiful in photographs, but this is one you truly have to see with your own eyes," the listing concludes.

After Newsom ends his term, he and his family are expected to move 90 miles west of the Sacramento home to Kentfield, Marin County, where they bought a home in 2024 for $9 million. Politico reported in 2024 that all four of the Newsoms' children were being enrolled in Marin County schools that year.

The family already lived in a different home in Kentfield before Newsom's electoral victory in 2018.

Newsweek contacted Newsom's office for comment by email on Tuesday morning.

Izzy Garson, a spokesperson for Newsom, told SFGate that "with the Governor's term ending in January 2027, the family began a gradual transition in 2024, purchasing a home in Marin County to provide continuity for their children's education. The sale of their Sacramento home is the next step in that transition."

Newsom is leaving office because, due to term limits, he cannot run for reelection. It is unclear who will succeed the Democratic governor in his Sacramento home—or in office, for that matter. The Golden State will hold an election to choose his successor on November 3, with Democrat Xavier Becerra and Republican Steve Hilton running.

Becerra currently leads Hilton 49.2 percent to 41 percent among 912 registered voters, with 9.8 percent undecided, according to a recent survey conducted August from 14 to 16 . The poll was commissioned by Hilton's campaign and conducted by David Wolfson, a pollster and faculty member in Columbia University's Political Analytics graduate program. It carries a 3.3-point margin of error and used MMS text-to-web methodology.

Contact Newsweek editors on this story: Matthew Cannon and James Debens

articles.title: Watchdog files bar complaint against Jeanine Pirro over bid to indict 6 Democratic lawmakers
articles.summary: A legal watchdog says it filed bar complaints on Tuesday accusing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro and two lieutenants of violating their ethical duties in seekin...
articles.body:
WASHINGTON (AP) — A legal watchdog says it filed bar complaints on Tuesday accusing U.S. Attorney Jeanine Pirro and two lieutenants of violating their ethical duties in seeking to charge six Democratic lawmakers with federal crimes for appearing in a video that called on troops to resist unlawful orders.

The Legal Accountability Center's bar complaints , filed in New York and Virginia, claim Pirro and her subordinates, Carlton Davis and Steven Vandervelden , abused their prosecutorial powers to seek "meritless" indictments against President Donald Trump's "perceived political enemies."

Tim Lauer, a spokesperson for Pirro's Washington-based office, noted that it's a grand jury's job — not prosecutors' — to decide whether to hand up an indictment.

"Attempting to weaponize the disciplinary process against prosecutors for doing their jobs amounts to nothing more than a frivolous complaint," Lauer said in a statement.

In February, a grand jury in Washington refused to indict Sens. Mark Kelly and Elissa Slotkin and four House Democrats for urging U.S. service members to follow established military protocols and reject orders they believe to be unlawful. All six lawmakers previously served in the military or at intelligence agencies. Trump accused them of sedition "punishable by DEATH" in a social media post.

A grand jury's refusal to return an indictment is extraordinarily rare, but it has become increasingly common in Washington during Trump's second term. Pirro's critics have accused her of pursuing other legally dubious and politically motivated cases at the Republican president's behest, such as the recently abandoned felony charge against a former Olympian who was accused of defacing the Lincoln Memorial Reflecting Pool.

The center has filed complaints against other Trump administration officials , including Ed Martin Jr. , Pirro's predecessor as U.S. Attorney for the District of Columbia. Martin has been a leading figure in Trump's campaign to use the Justice Department to prosecute his political opponents.

In its complaint against Pirro, the center asks bar officials to investigate whether she and her colleagues violated rules of professional conduct for attorneys — and to "pursue appropriate discipline" against them. Its complaint against Pirro says her office had no legal basis for its "patently improper effort" to secure an indictment against the six lawmakers.

"The only purpose could have been political animus and a desire to intimidate perceived enemies of the federal government and the President, who personally criticized the lawmakers' video as seditious and punishable by death," the complaint says.

Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth has tried to punish Kelly , a former Navy pilot representing Arizona, for participating in the video. Kelly sued in federal court to block the censure from Hegseth. A district court judge ruled in his favor . Hegseth has asked an appeals court to review the decision.

The center filed its complaint against Pirro and Vandervelden with a grievance committee based in White Plains, New York. In New York, the state Supreme Court's appellate division governs ethical complaints against attorneys. The center filed its complaint against Davis with the Virginia State Bar.

"Prosecutors have enormous power, and with that power comes an obligation to exercise independent legal judgment rather than use the criminal justice system to carry out a president's political demands," the center's co-founder, Michael Teter, said in a statement.

Pirro, who served as a county prosecutor and judge in New York, left her Fox News hosting job to become the top federal prosecutor for Washington last year.

articles.title: Trump doesn’t seem to care what people want anymore
articles.summary: When President Donald Trump took the political world by storm in 2016, his rise was often described as a “populist” one. He seems to have abandoned that bran...
articles.body:
When President Donald Trump took the political world by storm in 2016, his rise was often described as a "populist" one. And he certainly played the part of a renegade challenging a broken political system on behalf of regular Americans.

Ten years later, though, Trump has almost completely abandoned this brand of politics.

Indeed, in many ways, he has become the anti-populist .

And he's got the poll numbers to prove it.

Polling this month from Reuters and Ipsos has shown Trump's approval rating dropping to a record low of 33%. That's just 1 in 3 Americans who endorse his job performance.

But perhaps more telling is the still-falling percentage who "strongly" approve of him. It's been dropping for a while now . And in the newest poll, it's at just 13% of all Americans and 35% of Republicans .

That's roughly 1 in 8 Americans who think what Trump is doing is great — a remarkably small number of truly devoted supporters. And despite the president's supposed hammerlock on his base, nearly two-thirds of Republicans are less than enthused.

So how does a president get to that point?

For Trump, it's by almost totally disregarding public opinion in favor of his own whims, desires and even personal enrichment and glorification — a propensity he seems inclined to continue even during the stretch run of the midterms, when many politicians are highly sensitive to what plays well with voters.

Trump's threatened 50% tariffs on Canada are a case in point.

A CNN poll this spring showed 65% of Americans said Trump's tariffs had a negative impact on their personal finances. And even when the tariffs as a whole weren't as unpopular last year, his initial Canada levies were still very unpopular; between 60% and 64% of Americans opposed them from the outset.

So what does Trump do 70 days before the midterms? Embrace a trade war with Canada, naturally.

Trump on Tuesday even threatened to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America as part of the feud — echoing his purported renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. Around two-thirds of Americans also opposed the latter change.

Vice President JD Vance got in on the act Monday by mislabeling Canada as a "state" and calling it a "Freudian slip" — evoking Trump's threats to make Canada the 51st state. And why not? A Marquette University Law School poll last year, after all, showed 75% of Americans opposed this idea.

Trump's recent positive comments about data centers are also perplexing for a supposed populist.

There is perhaps no more clear-cut populist issue right now than opposing data centers. As many as 7 in 10 Americans oppose having them in their communities, largely perceiving the centers as something powerful tech companies are inflicting upon them.

But even as his fellow Republicans turn sharply against them, Trump is embracing them . He's calling data centers "big, strong, bold, and Money Machines" and "Cash Cows." He said communities should welcome them and praised their architecture as the "most incredible buildings I've ever seen." He's even criticized Republicans for supporting moratoriums that ban data center development.

But these are hardly the only examples of Trump's anti-populism:

Polls show 6 in 10 Americans say Trump has "gone too far" in changing institutions like the Kennedy Center, and just 9% of Americans think it's appropriate to name government buildings after Trump while he's still president. Yet Trump is again trying to slap his name on the Kennedy Center.

He continues to focus extensively on his renovations of DC — often parading them for the cameras like he did with the new White House helipad Monday. This despite a Washington Post poll last month showing Americans viewed these kinds of projects negatively by a 2-to-1 margin.

The Iran war was clearly not what Americans wanted from the start; they opposed intervention by 2-to-1 margins in prewar polls. And Trump's supposed anti-war streak was core to his populism. Yet six months after launching the war, Trump is now threatening to extend the conflict through the midterms.

He's continued his factually deprived assault on vaccines this month, even as KFF polling shows 6 in 10 Americans oppose the administration's handling of the issue.

Trump until a few weeks ago seemingly wouldn't let go of his $1.776 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, which the White House has said could send money to violent January 6, 2021, defendants. This despite a poll last year showing 83% of Americans opposed Trump decision to pardon those people — much less paying them.

The problem with most of those examples isn't just that Trump is focused on his unpopular pet projects. It's that he's focused on them to the exclusion of and often at the expense of what people really want, which is a laser focus on affordability and economic issues.

He instead repeatedly talks about how we're in an economic "golden age," even though just 4% of Americans in the new Reuters-Ipsos poll said the economy was "very strong."

And people have noticed, with polls showing overwhelming majorities believe that he's neglecting the most important issues like inflation.

It all begs the question: What do voters do when a president basically casts off even the veneer of interest in doing what the people want — and instead does a series of things he wants that even large segments of his base appear uncomfortable with ?

It sets up a pretty remarkable test of partisanship in the 2026 midterms.

For more CNN news and newsletters create an account at CNN.com
paragraphs: When President Donald Trump took the political world by storm in 2016, his rise was often described as a "populist" one. And he certainly played the part of a renegade challenging a broken political system on behalf of regular Americans.
Ten years later, though, Trump has almost completely abandoned this brand of politics.
Indeed, in many ways, he has become the anti-populist .
And he's got the poll numbers to prove it.
Polling this month from Reuters and Ipsos has shown Trump's approval rating dropping to a record low of 33%. That's just 1 in 3 Americans who endorse his job performance.

But perhaps more telling is the still-falling percentage who "strongly" approve of him. It's been dropping for a while now . And in the newest poll, it's at just 13% of all Americans and 35% of Republicans .

That's roughly 1 in 8 Americans who think what Trump is doing is great — a remarkably small number of truly devoted supporters. And despite the president's supposed hammerlock on his base, nearly two-thirds of Republicans are less than enthused.
So how does a president get to that point?

For Trump, it's by almost totally disregarding public opinion in favor of his own whims, desires and even personal enrichment and glorification — a propensity he seems inclined to continue even during the stretch run of the midterms, when many politicians are highly sensitive to what plays well with voters.
Trump's threatened 50% tariffs on Canada are a case in point.

A CNN poll this spring showed 65% of Americans said Trump's tariffs had a negative impact on their personal finances. And even when the tariffs as a whole weren't as unpopular last year, his initial Canada levies were still very unpopular; between 60% and 64% of Americans opposed them from the outset.
So what does Trump do 70 days before the midterms? Embrace a trade war with Canada, naturally.

Trump on Tuesday even threatened to change the name of Lake Ontario to Lake America as part of the feud — echoing his purported renaming of the Gulf of Mexico as the Gulf of America. Around two-thirds of Americans also opposed the latter change.

Vice President JD Vance got in on the act Monday by mislabeling Canada as a "state" and calling it a "Freudian slip" — evoking Trump's threats to make Canada the 51st state. And why not? A Marquette University Law School poll last year, after all, showed 75% of Americans opposed this idea.
Trump's recent positive comments about data centers are also perplexing for a supposed populist.

There is perhaps no more clear-cut populist issue right now than opposing data centers. As many as 7 in 10 Americans oppose having them in their communities, largely perceiving the centers as something powerful tech companies are inflicting upon them.

But even as his fellow Republicans turn sharply against them, Trump is embracing them . He's calling data centers "big, strong, bold, and Money Machines" and "Cash Cows." He said communities should welcome them and praised their architecture as the "most incredible buildings I've ever seen." He's even criticized Republicans for supporting moratoriums that ban data center development.
But these are hardly the only examples of Trump's anti-populism:

Polls show 6 in 10 Americans say Trump has "gone too far" in changing institutions like the Kennedy Center, and just 9% of Americans think it's appropriate to name government buildings after Trump while he's still president. Yet Trump is again trying to slap his name on the Kennedy Center.

He continues to focus extensively on his renovations of DC — often parading them for the cameras like he did with the new White House helipad Monday. This despite a Washington Post poll last month showing Americans viewed these kinds of projects negatively by a 2-to-1 margin.

The Iran war was clearly not what Americans wanted from the start; they opposed intervention by 2-to-1 margins in prewar polls. And Trump's supposed anti-war streak was core to his populism. Yet six months after launching the war, Trump is now threatening to extend the conflict through the midterms.
He's continued his factually deprived assault on vaccines this month, even as KFF polling shows 6 in 10 Americans oppose the administration's handling of the issue.

Trump until a few weeks ago seemingly wouldn't let go of his $1.776 billion "anti-weaponization" fund, which the White House has said could send money to violent January 6, 2021, defendants. This despite a poll last year showing 83% of Americans opposed Trump decision to pardon those people — much less paying them.

The problem with most of those examples isn't just that Trump is focused on his unpopular pet projects. It's that he's focused on them to the exclusion of and often at the expense of what people really want, which is a laser focus on affordability and economic issues.
He instead repeatedly talks about how we're in an economic "golden age," even though just 4% of Americans in the new Reuters-Ipsos poll said the economy was "very strong."
And people have noticed, with polls showing overwhelming majorities believe that he's neglecting the most important issues like inflation.

It all begs the question: What do voters do when a president basically casts off even the veneer of interest in doing what the people want — and instead does a series of things he wants that even large segments of his base appear uncomfortable with ?
It sets up a pretty remarkable test of partisanship in the 2026 midterms.

articles.title: Abdul El-Sayed pushes back in Fox News interview: ‘Not here to fight a culture war’
articles.summary: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, tangled with Fox News host Jesse Watters in an interview Monday, repeatedly pivoting from “culture war” questions to refocus on affordability in his state.
articles.body: Abdul El-Sayed, the Democratic nominee for Senate in Michigan, tangled with Fox News host Jesse Watters in an interview Monday, repeatedly pivoting from “culture war” questions to refocus on affordability in his state. “You want to bring up all this culture war,” El-Sayed told Watters during the 25-minute interview. “I’m not here to fight a culture war. I’m here to fight the affordability crisis that people are facing.” Watters pressed the nominee on several hot-button topics in the combative but largely jovial interview, including whether he supports abolishing Immigration and Customs Enforcement, Shariah, gender reassignment surgery, and whether “men should play women’s sports.” On the ICE question, El-Sayed painted the agency as brutal and ineffective. “You and I both know that we’ve, long before we ever had ICE, we had INS,” he said, referring to the agency that predated ICE, the U.S. Immigration and Naturalization Service. “We were able to enforce our immigration policies without shooting people in the face and the back of the head. The INS worked a lot better.” El-Sayed added that immigration isn’t at the top of Michiganders’ minds. “When I travel the state, and I have traveled my state, more people are asking me about how they’re going to afford their gas and groceries. They’re not asking me about immigration,” he said. Asked about electric cars, the candidate said the “bigger question” is “why the president just started a trade war or escalated a trade war with Canada. It’s about to make all of our cars, especially the internal combustion engine cars, so much more expensive.” El-Sayed used that same question to advocate for hiking taxes on people making over $100 million. “Do you want to drive on good roads, or would you rather have a billionaire make a second billion? That’s what Mike Rogers wants,” he said, referring to his Republican opponent. “That’s what Donald Trump wants. Apparently, that’s what you want. I think the people in Michigan want something different. They want good roads and good schools.” “I just think I have the right to the fruits of my own labor,” Watters responded. El-Sayed, who would be the first Muslim senator if elected in November, took a more libertarian tack when pushed on religious laws for Muslims and transgender issues. “So, canon law is the name for Christian law,” he said. “I don’t begrudge you your right to practice your faith as you choose. I don’t know why the idea that I could practice my faith as I choose is a problem. Nobody is trying to push Shariah law on anyone else. Just like I hope nobody is trying to push canon law on anybody else, because we live in an America where you should have the freedom of your religion.” “The issue that people are worried about is not that somehow somebody’s going to come and push Shariah law on them,” he continued. “The issue in Michigan is people are worried about how they’re going to afford their gas. The issue in Michigan is ‘How am I going to see a doctor when I get sick?’ ‘How am I going to keep my job?’” After a brief exchange on whether El-Sayed thinks the NFL is racist, prompting him to simply complain about high ticket prices, Watters then asked, “Sex changes for minors, do you support that?” “I just think the government shouldn’t tell you what kind of healthcare you should have,” El-Sayed answered. When the news anchor asked if the candidate thinks “it’s OK for a parent to slash his kid’s ding-a-ling off,” he responded, “Do you really want to have this conversation? Are you circumcised?” Watters answered in the affirmative and called it a “personal question.” “It’s a problem that you think that you get to decide what happens between a parent, a doctor and a patient,” El-Sayed said. “I’m just saying that yes, circumcision is surgery on a kid’s ding-a-ling. So if you really want to bring that up, you can. I just think you guys are really selective about these things.” Watters called the response “wacky” and “sick stuff.” On whether men should “play women’s sports,” El-Sayed said he thinks that also is not an issue for the government. “At the end of the day, the decision of who gets to play what sports ought to be decided by the people who govern sports,” he responded. “I’m running for U.S. Senate, Jesse. It’s insane. I’m out here trying to take on, like, the healthcare crisis and Big Pharma, and you’re asking me about who gets to play what sports.” Watters wrapped up the interview by thanking El-Sayed for coming on and saying he’d be invited back. “You seem a little naive, Abdul. I give you credit for facing the music, but some of the stuff’s just straight-up wacky,” Watters said. “You know, I don’t know if that’s going to fly in Michigan.”
